content:
carmen: Hey @people-ops — heads up I'm planning to work from France for ~11 months (2026-09-15 -> 2027-08-14). Want to confirm impact on WFH stipend, health coverage, and retirement contributions. Also: do I need a French social security number?

nora-peopleops: hi Carmen :wave: thanks for the heads up. short answer: >90 days triggers temporary work abroad workflow. France has strong social security rules; 11 months will likely require cross-border review. please start the Temporary Work Abroad form: https://docs.company/temporary-work-abroad and put actual dates.

carmen: done — form submitted just now. What's the typical treatment for the monthly WFH stipend for ~11 months?

jill-benefits: hi — stipend policy: for temporary stays >6 months we usually convert to country-adjusted stipend or reimburse coworking via expenses. France has VAT/different invoicing rules so we often reimburse with receipts. we'll run estimate and post guidance in the ticket.

sam-payroll: FYI payroll note: if local authorities determine you are subject to French social contributions, we either (A) run payroll through our French payroll partner or (B) maintain US payroll but with local reporting. Option A means US 401(k) deferrals will pause; Option B may still require employer social charges. We'll perform a withholding/residency check once HR provides the dates and location.

ben-legal: adding legal flag: France can treat remote work as creating employer obligations if the employee is habitually working there and the company has any economic activity. For <12 months it's usually manageable, but we need to confirm no local permanent establishment risk. I'll run a short assessment after payroll flags.

carmen: what about health insurance? I'm currently on US group plan. Will that continue?

jill-benefits: If you remain on US payroll, international medical coverage may continue but local providers may not accept it. If moved onto French payroll, you'll be enrolled in French social security / assurance maladie and our US plan may be terminated. We can arrange a continuity short-term private plan if needed — I'll DM you a cost estimate and options.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: for assignments >90 days, submit passport + local address + emergency contact to People Ops. See: https://confluence.company/travel-remote-policy

carmen: thanks. Also: I have a company laptop — do I need to ship it or is it okay to bring? Any import/export tax issues?

nora-peopleops: Usually fine for short-term travel. Bring the laptop and keep a copy of company asset docs. For stays >6 months in some countries there can be customs formalities; France typically allows temporary import but keep serial + invoice handy. If you plan to buy local equipment we can approve reimbursements.

tom-manager: Approving coworking receipts up to €120/month for Carmen while abroad. Carmen, ping me in the ticket when you have receipts.

carmen: great, thanks Tom. Last Q: do I need to change my `home_base` in Rippling now or later?

sam-payroll: Change `home_base` only if you will be permanently relocating. For temporary assignments we leave `home_base` as-is and mark the assignment in payroll as "temp abroad". That avoids switching benefits unless local payroll cutover is required.

ben-legal: We'll aim to complete the assessment within 10 business days after payroll receives the form. If any local payroll is required we'll coordinate timing to minimize disruption.

carmen: appreciate it — I'll upload passport + address and drop receipts in Concur. Thank you everyone :slightly_smiling_face:
